podcast.title: Career Breakthrough with "Old Town Road" (2019)
podcast.body: In 2018, Montero Lamar Hill, then a struggling rapper contemplating quitting music after dropping out of college, found a beat online for $30 from Dutch producer Young Kio. He rapped over it, released "Old Town Road" independently, and its unexpected success via the "Yeehaw Challenge" meme launched him into mainstream pop stardom and secured a deal with Columbia Records. "In 2018, a failing rapper named Montero Lamar Hill was about to give up on a career in music."

podcast.title: Cultural Reinforcement through Yeehaw Agenda (2019)
podcast.body: As 2019 began, "Old Town Road" became the official soundtrack of the "Yeehaw Agenda" across social media. This mutually reinforcing relationship broadened the black cowboy cultural conversation into both a meme and a social movement. "What was mutually reinforcing about the agenda and the Yeehaw challenge was the broadening of the black cowboy cultural conversation into both a meme and a kind of social movement."

podcast.title: Promotional Appearances (2019)
podcast.body: To maintain the song's cross-cultural and viral momentum, Lil Nas X made various public appearances in his cowboy outfit. These included sporting events, awards shows, the Stagecoach Festival, and even an elementary school. "He appeared in his cowboy outfit at sporting events, awards shows, the Stage Coach Festival, even an elementary school."

podcast.title: Record-Setting Hit (2019)
podcast.body: In 2019, "Old Town Road" set an all-time Hot 100 record. Its success stemmed from a combination of remixes, a multi-genre audience, viral videos, social media dominance, Montero's public coming out, and the song's infectious quality. "Old Town Road set an all-time hot 100 record."

podcast.title: 2020 Grammy Awards Triumph
podcast.body: At the 2020 Grammy Awards, "Old Town Road" won two prizes. Lil Nas X performed the mega smash live on stage with a full band, a string section, and many collaborators who contributed to its success, including BTS, Diplo, Mason Ramsey, and Billy Ray Cyrus. The performance highlighted the song's evolution from a self-produced internet beat to a supersized live event, marking a triumph where the song felt like it "belonged to everybody." "At the 2020 Grammys Old Town Road took home two prizes and Lil Nas X performed his improbable mega smash with the help of a full band, a string section and almost everybody who had helped him make it a smash. BTS, Diplo, Mason Ramsey and Billy Ray Cyrus."

podcast.body: The host personally would have awarded Lil Nas X the Album of the Year Grammy in 2022, instead of Jon Batiste's "We Are," indicating a preference for more current and charting artists. "I would have given Batista some smaller prizes that year and given the big prize to Lil Nas X or Olivia Rodrigo."

podcast.title: Major Label Music Video - "Official Movie"
podcast.body: Columbia Records released a major label music video for "Old Town Road," which they dubbed "the official movie." This video garnered tens of millions of views and featured cameos from various artists and personalities, including rapper Vince Staples, remixer Diplo, co-star Billy Ray Cyrus, and comedian Chris Rock. "The release of the song's major label music video which Columbia Records called the official movie. Racked up tens of millions of views and featured cameos from rapper Vince Staples, remixer Diplo, of course co-star Billy Ray Cyrus and even Chris Rock."

xref.title: Songwriting Credit on "Old Town Road" (2019)
xref.body: Trent Reznor holds the record for the most weeks at the top of the Billboard Hot 100 singles chart due to his songwriting credit on Lil Nas X's "Old Town Road." His involvement stemmed from the song's beat sampling the instrumental track "34 Ghosts 4" from Nine Inch Nails' 2008 album "Ghosts I–IV," with Reznor granting permission for the sample and receiving credit alongside his songwriting partner Atticus Ross. "Trent listened to Old Town Road and declared it to be unbelievably catchy, so he said, yeah, go ahead and use it, but I need a songwriting credit, which is very reasonable."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 3: (80-71)

xref.title: Songwriting Credit on "Old Town Road" (2019)
xref.body: Atticus Ross received a songwriting credit for Lil Nas X's "Old Town Road" alongside Trent Reznor, Montero Hill (Lil Nas X), and Kioa Rokima (Young Kio). This credit stemmed from the song's use of a sample from Nine Inch Nails' instrumental "34 Ghosts 4," with Ross benefiting from the song's immense global success, including 18 million copies sold and billions of streams. "the songwriting credits for Old Town Road, you'll see that the writers are listed as Montero Hill, Kioa Rokima, the real name of Young Kio, plus Trent Risener and his songwriting partner Atticus Ross."

xref.title: Co-holder of Billboard Hot 100 Record
xref.body: As co-composer of "34 Ghosts 4," the source material for Lil Nas X's "Old Town Road," Trent Reznor (with Atticus Ross) shares the record for the pop song with the most weeks (19) at number one on the Billboard Hot 100. "So yes, Trent Rezner is the co-holder of the record for the pop song, the pop song, with the most weeks at number one on Billboard."

xref.title: Dutch Beatmaker and Old Town Road
xref.body: This Dutch beatmaker remixed the Nine Inch Nails instrumental track "34 Ghosts 4" and sold the result online for $30. This remix was then purchased by Montero Hill (Lil Nas X) and became the basis for "Old Town Road." "A Dutch beatmaker named Young Kiel took up Trent on his offer. He messed with one of the tracks called 34 Ghosts 4 and put the results up for sale online for $30."

xref.title: Impact on Lil Nas X
xref.body: Trent Reznor accidentally contributed to Lil Nas X becoming a major pop star when the latter used a remixed instrumental track from Nine Inch Nails' "Ghosts I–IV" for his hit song "Old Town Road." "And he accidentally turned Lil Nas X into one of the biggest pop stars in the planet."

xref.title: Producer of "Old Town Road" Beat
xref.body: Young Kio, a Dutch record producer, created the beat for Lil Nas X's "Old Town Road" by manipulating a sample from Nine Inch Nails' instrumental track "34 Ghosts 4" and selling it for $30 on his online store, where Lil Nas X purchased it. His real name is Kioa Rokima. "He stumbled upon a track called 34 Ghosts 4, an instrumental from the 2008 Nine-H Nails album Ghost 1-4."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 3: (80-71)

xref.title: Producer of "Old Town Road" Beat
xref.body: Young Kioh, a Dutch producer, created the beat for Lil Nas X's "Old Town Road" based on Nine Inch Nails' "34 Ghosts 4." Lil Nas X purchased this beat online for $30. Young Kioh was unaware of the beat's use until the song became a massive hit. Through a quiet negotiation, he received songwriting credits, a share of the profits, and shared in the Grammy wins for the song. "He found a Dutch kid by the name of Young Kioh, who had created a beat based on a track called 34 Ghosts 4."

This granted them a share of the profits and Grammy wins for the record-breaking single. "Trent and his songwriting partner, Atticus Ross, were given songwriting credits on Old Town Road and thus a share of the profits."
